heroLead: Purple Sage is a small residential community outside Rock Springs, sitting on the same railroad checkerboard that runs through the rest of Sweetwater County.
intro: Like much of this stretch of the county, Purple Sage sits near the historic Union Pacific grant pattern, and mineral ownership on any given tract can trace back either to private railroad-grant land or, on the alternating sections, to federal minerals administered by the BLM. We check that specifically before making an offer, since it determines whether there is even a private interest to buy.

Because the community grew up as a residential area outside Rock Springs rather than a mining or drilling camp, a lot of the mineral files we see here are legacy interests held by families who never lived on the land itself — often passed down from an earlier generation that owned a larger tract before it was broken up.

sections.heading: Confirming private versus federal minerals
paragraphs: The single most important step for a Purple Sage-area file is confirming which section your legal description falls in. Odd-numbered railroad-grant sections carry private mineral rights that changed hands many times over the decades; even sections are typically federal.

sections.heading: Nearby gas activity
paragraphs: The Rock Springs uplift's gas production extends into parts of this area. If your tract is inside an active unit, current production history factors directly into our offer.

sections.heading: What to send
paragraphs: A division order, check stub, or the legal description from your deed is what we need to start the review.

faqs.question: I'm not sure if my minerals are federal or private. How do I find out?
faqs.answer: Send us your legal description and we will check it against the historic checkerboard pattern and current BLM records.

faqs.question: Is there current drilling activity near Purple Sage?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific unit. We check current state filings before making an offer.

faqs.question: What if I only have an old lease from a relative?
faqs.answer: That's enough to start. We trace ownership from there through county and state records.

faqs.question: Does it matter that I've never lived near Purple Sage myself?
faqs.answer: No. A lot of the mineral owners we work with here inherited the interest without ever living on or near the land, and that has no bearing on what you're able to sell.

faqs.question: How quickly can this close once we agree on a number?
faqs.answer: Once title is confirmed, closing on a Purple Sage-area interest typically moves faster than a larger, more complicated tract because the file work is usually straightforward.
